title: Native control styles
notes: Use native Button, TextField, Toggle, and Label with our style adapters. Formatting, enum-based focus, roles, keyboard shortcuts, and submission remain SwiftUI APIs. Pass explicit focus state to the style for focus appearance. CNFieldControl decorates native controls that do not have a matching style protocol. Convenience components share the same recipes and styling engine. Change CNField.axis to move the label above or beside the same control group. AnyLayout preserves the children; .tw("feedback-motion", value: horizontal) supplies motion. Group the editor and supporting text so they remain together in both orientations.

title: Native drawer content
notes: CNDrawerContent applies the drawer recipe to a vertical stack. It adds no scrolling, fixed size, or presentation host. Use it inside your own sheet to control detents, drag indicators, interactive dismissal, appearance, and callbacks. Keep the selected detent in the supported set. Detents follow platform behavior; macOS sheets use native window sizing. CNDrawer supplies scrolling, appearance, and nested hosts, with typed detents, selection, and onDismiss arguments. A caller-owned sheet also owns nested hosts and dismissal scope. Use the sheet binding or a native dismiss action to close it; clear cnPresentationDismiss if you reuse CNDialogClose inside a native sheet nested in a custom dialog.

title: Adaptive surfaces and Liquid Glass
notes:
State the role and let swiftcn choose the native appearance. surface-floating uses Liquid Glass on iOS 26 and macOS 26, a material with a themed edge on earlier systems, and a solid themed surface under Reduce Transparency. surface-solid always uses the theme. glass asks for glass explicitly and uses the same fallbacks. Each surface resolves to one fill, so bg-* selects the solid color and never stacks under glass or a material. .twAppearance(.automatic | .glass | .solid) sets the policy for a subtree; local classes still win.

.buttonStyle(.tw("glass")) lets Apple draw the Button: it selects .glass or .glassProminent where available, or .bordered and .borderedProminent before. Its classes add spacing and typography to the label, not another background. TWSurfaceGroup wraps GlassEffectContainer and twSurfaceID wraps glassEffectID, so grouping and morphing stay explicit. twPresentationSurface keeps the system sheet where it uses glass and applies the theme surface elsewhere.

Accessibility and policy changes alter values inside a fixed view structure, so editors, bindings, and focus remain. Keep a view's surface role constant; changing between a surface class and none rebuilds the content. glass-interactive enables Apple's touch and pointer feedback only. Classes never install gestures; custom drag and scroll handoff remains component code.

title: Native navigation
notes: Use NavigationSplitView, List, and NavigationLink directly for app navigation. The sidebar-list and sidebar-item-label recipes supply appearance. SwiftUI owns column visibility, selected-row appearance, keyboard navigation, and compact navigation. Label parts preserve the native link; avoid putting action buttons inside a navigation link. Keep editor state in the caller. CNSidebar remains the separate icon-rail and offcanvas layout. The gallery opens this example as a complete navigation root. Set a flexible navigationSplitViewColumnWidth(min:ideal:max:) on each column to choose a useful resize range. The minimum detail width protects the editor. SwiftUI still controls compact presentation and sidebar visibility.

title: Native split views
notes: Use HSplitView or VSplitView on macOS and apply .tw to their panes. SwiftUI owns the dividers; native frames or sizing classes define minimum pane sizes. Native split views do not expose a SwiftUI fraction binding. CNResizable supplies that explicit binding and the mobile touch handle. Keep state outside the panes so resizing preserves native editors and controls. Give each desktop pane a flexible maximum width with w-full as well as a minimum width. A minimum-only frame can pin a pane to its intrinsic width. Use native frame alignment to keep the pane content leading-aligned while it grows.

title: Native arrangements
notes: Use ArrangementView on iOS 27.1 or macOS 27.1 for two related panes. SwiftUI chooses their placement around active divisions. Keep navigation outside the arrangement. Put each pane's scrolling content inside the arrangement. Keep shared state in the screen. Apply .tw to the native content. The example uses AnyLayout on older systems and opens as a complete screen in the gallery. Compile the new API with Xcode 27.1 or later. The package keeps its iOS 17 and macOS 14 deployment targets.

title: Observable models and custom content
notes:
Own an @Observable model with @State. Use @Bindable in a child form to pass typed bindings to native controls and swiftcn components. The model controls validation and saving.

CNCommand accepts a query binding and generic itemContent and empty builders. Keep each item builder as a native button label; put additional actions outside that label.

CNToastHost.toastContent changes a card body while the host retains stacking, dismissal, and deadlines. context.action creates a native button that pauses the deadline during keyboard or accessibility focus. Custom controls can use context.focus and context.accessibilityFocus with a stable UUID. context.dismiss removes only the current toast value. Keep plain @State for local component values.
